meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-30 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Redwood: Ethan Morales (AE), Priya Nandakumar (SE)
Stonegate: Mark Redding (Head of AI), Lena Ortiz (Security Lead), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Tara Kim (Legal)
summary: Intro and qualification of Stonegate's security posture, evaluation criteria for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, detailed questions on SOC2/ISO, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, audit logs retention, and customer-managed KMS/HSM. Redwood outlined fallback strategies, data residency options, and pilot next steps. Action items assigned for security artifacts and pilot planning.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 status
RBAC and least privilege model for inference endpoints
Audit logs, observability, and retention windows
Encryption and KMS options (customer-managed keys, HSM)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency)
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the hour. I'm Ethan with Redwood, AE on this account.
[00:06] Priya: Hi, Priya here - I'm a solutions engineer, I'll jump in on the infra and KMS questions.
[00:10] Mark: Thanks, Ethan, Priya. Mark Redding here - I lead the AI org at Stonegate. Lena and Samir are with me.
[00:16] Lena: Hi all. Quick note, Tara from legal is listening in to spot any compliance flags.
[00:20] Samir: Samir, platform eng. we'll be doing the integration work.
[00:24] Ethan: Great. High level, we want to understand your constraints — security, controls, and what's driving your Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision. Can you frame your top priorities?
[00:34] Mark: Absolutely. For us it's four things: 1) data residency and isolation for PII, 2) ability to manage keys (we prefer CMKs), 3) auditability — long retention on logs, and 4) predictable latency for customer-facing features. Cost is important but secondary.
[00:52] Priya: Got it. On keys, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and bring-your-own-key options, and also HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with CMK support — we can walk through the exact flow.
[01:10] Lena: That's helpful. For SOC2/ISO — do you have Type II and ISO 27001? We need to know what evidence you can share.
[01:18] Ethan: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified — we can share the report links and a redacted pen test summary. I'll send those after the call.
[01:25] Tara: From legal: can you confirm whether audit logs contain PII or whether they are redacted? Our policy is to avoid PII in logs.
[01:34] Priya: By default, audit logs capture metadata (request id, model used, latency, tokens) but customers can opt out of storing prompts or set redaction rules. In Dedicated/Private, you control whether request payloads are persisted.
[01:50] Samir: Important note — if we run on Hosted but with CMK, who has access to the plaintext keys? We require that only our ops can rotate and hold keys.
[01:58] Ethan: For CMK on Hosted, the key is customer-managed in your AWS account (if using our VPC/private offering) or we can do a customer-managed key but hosted in our cloud — with strict role separation. We'll document access model.
[02:12] Mark: Ok. Can you explain the difference in isolation between Dedicated and Private? I want to make sure we don't misinterpret dedicated pool as same as fully private.
[02:22] Priya: Good question. Redwood Dedicated means reserved GPU pools provisioned for you — compute is single-tenant but control plane is still hosted. Private means the control plane is in your VPC or on-prem; complete separation including audit, logs, and keys under your tenancy. Dedicated is right fit if you need isolation and predictable throughput but can accept our control plane. Private is for strict regulatory or data residency needs.
[02:46] Lena: For Private, do you support in-country deployments? We have EU and APAC constraints.
[02:51] Priya: Yes, we support regional Private deployments and can work with partners for on-prem installs in special cases.
[02:58] Mark: Latency targets — we need 95th p95 under 200ms for short prompts. Can Dedicated hit that?
[03:05] Priya: Depends on model and batch config. With Dedicated, you get pinned capacity and can tune batching/kv-cache. For MPT-like open models on A100/whatever, hitting p95 under 200ms for <512 tokens is feasible; we'll verify in pilot.
[03:20] Samir: We've previously seen some vendor doc say 'KV cache' and the service would leak prompt prefixes into logs — clarity on what gets cached and for how long?
[03:29] Priya: The KV cache is per request session to accelerate generation; it doesn't leave the instance unless you enable persistence. For security-sensitive flows you can disable K V cache sharing and use single-use sessions.
[03:38] Mark: On SSO — we use Okta and SCIM provisioning. How deep is your SAML support? Do you have Just-In-Time provisioning?
[03:46] Ethan: We support SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with role sync. JIT provisioning is supported for small teams; for enterprise we recommend SCIM.
[03:56] Lena: RBAC model: can we define least privilege per route, per model, and per token? We want dev/test separation and production roles.
[04:04] Priya: Yes — our RBAC supports per-route and per-model policies, API key scoping, and token scoping. In Dedicated/Private you can integrate with your identity provider for role mapping.
[04:14] Tara: Any SOC2 audit trails for modifications to RBAC or key rotations? We need immutable logs for changes to IAM and KMS.
[04:22] Priya: Change events to RBAC, key usage logs, and rotation events are recorded in the audit trail; retention depends on plan but can be extended for enterprise customers. We'll include retention tiers in the doc.
[04:35] Mark: What's your default retention for audit logs and model inputs on Hosted?
[04:40] Ethan: Defaults are: aggregated metadata 13 months, more detailed traces including prompts 90 days unless you opt-in to longer retention. For Dedicated/Private you set retention policy.
[04:50] Lena: We probably need 1 year for metadata and 90 days for payloads — but legal might push for 7 years on certain logs. Is that feasible?
[04:58] Priya: We can support extended retention for metadata up to 7 years for enterprise agreements; payload retention is configurable but generally we recommend minimizing unnecessary storage of PII.
[05:10] Samir: For encryption at rest and in transit — TLS is fine but do you support FIPS-validated cipher suites and HSM-backed root keys?
[05:18] Priya: Yes, TLS 1.2/1.3 with FIPS ciphers can be enabled. HSM-backed root keys are available for Private deployments or BYOK setups that require HSM.
[05:26] Mark: If we do a pilot on Dedicated, what are the steps? We want to bring a small traffic slice, run latency and cost baselines, and validate SSO + RBAC + KMS integration.
[05:36] Priya: Typical pilot: 1) share traffic profile and prompts, 2) Redwood provisions a Dedicated pool, 3) run 1–2 weeks of load/latency tests and security checks, 4) jointly review logs and retention settings. We'll prepare a checklist.
[05:50] Ethan: I'll capture that in the next steps. We'll also send the security deck and SOC2 artifacts.
[05:56] Mark: One red flag — we need to know whether your hosted model catalog includes any models that phone home or have telemetry. We don't want data ETL outside of our tenancy.
[06:06] Priya: We vet models; by default, Hosted models do not phone home. For absolute control, Private is recommended. We'll include model vetting notes.
[06:15] Lena: About production incident response — do you offer runbooks and paging for Dedicated?
[06:20] Ethan: We provide SLOs and an on-call escalation for enterprise Dedicated customers; runbooks and playbooks can be shared under an NDA.
[06:27] Samir: How do you handle GDPR subject access requests if model logs contain user prompts?
[06:33] Priya: In Hosted, we can locate and purge user data on request where it's stored — we treat prompts as customer data and will assist. Private gives you full control for compliance.
[06:43] Mark: Any restrictions on embeddings? We want to store embeddings long-term for search features — how do you treat embeddings from a data governance standpoint?
[06:51] Priya: Embeddings are data like any other; you can choose retention and encryption. If you need to keep them indefinitely, Dedicated or Private with your KMS is recommended.
[06:59] Lena: A quick question on legal: if we invoice Redwood and we need a DPA with sub-processors list, can you give that?
[07:06] Ethan: Yes, we'll share our DPA and subprocessor list; Tara we can set a follow-up to go deeper on contract language.
[07:14] Tara: Great. We also need proof of separation for multi-tenant metadata — e.g., how do you guarantee no co-mingling?
[07:21] Priya: For Dedicated we guarantee isolated compute and namespace separation; metadata may still be aggregated in the control plane unless Private is chosen. We'll add a diagram showing tenant boundaries.
[07:32] Mark: There was mention earlier of rate limiting and quotas — do those get audited? For compliance we need to know where throttling events are recorded.
[07:40] Priya: Throttling, rate limit events, and denied requests are part of observability and are logged. Retention policy applies.
[07:46] Ethan: I want to call out two common traps: 1) assuming CMK means zero provider visibility — you should validate key usage logs and rotation policy, and 2) assuming Dedicated removes all control plane telemetry — it reduces it but control plane still reports metrics.
[08:02] Mark: Understood. Can you show an example of the audit log record? Even redacted?
[08:08] Priya: We'll attach a sample export in the follow-up. It will have fields like request_id, user_id (redacted), model, tokens_in/out, latency, and change events.
[08:19] Samir: On the network side, for VPC peering, do you support private endpoints and strict egress rules?
[08:25] Priya: Yes. We support private endpoints, VPC peering, and allow listing egress destinations.
[08:31] Mark: About backups and snapshots for on-prem Private — do you do encrypted snapshots with customer keys?
[08:36] Priya: Snapshots can be encrypted with customer keys for Private deployments. We'll map this in the runbook.
[08:43] Lena: If we enable prompt redaction, is there any model-quality tradeoff? We need to ensure redaction doesn't break context for generation.
[08:50] Priya: It depends. Redacting PII might remove signals; we recommend token-level redaction with preserving structure, or a hybrid where sensitive fields are replaced with placeholders. We can run tests in the pilot to evaluate quality delta.
[09:02] Mark: Great. Let's talk timeline — we want a decision in Q4. Pilot in early Oct if possible.
[09:09] Ethan: That's doable. We'll aim to provision a pilot the week of Oct 12.
[09:14] Tara: On contracts — standard terms are fine but we'll need SLA language for Dedicated and liability caps clarified.
[09:20] Ethan: Noted. We'll include sample SLA language in the package.
[09:25] Samir: Another technical nit — are model weights ever stored outside the instance? Are there third party telemetry or analytics baked into the runtime?
[09:34] Priya: Model weights are part of the runtime image; no external telemetry from model weights. Any analytics collected is for service ops and is summarized metadata; we can provide opt-outs for pilot.
[09:44] Mark: Okay, let's move to quick live questions from the team — Lena?
[09:48] Lena: For key rotation, what's the frequency and is rollback possible? We want automated rotation every 90 days and ability to revoke quickly.
[09:56] Priya: We support scheduled rotation and emergency revocation. For CMK, rotations are in customer's KMS. For provider keys we can schedule rotation and keep key versions to allow graceful rollover.
[10:06] Lena: And who can trigger rotations — only admins? Need audit trail.
[10:11] Priya: Yes, RBAC controls who can trigger rotations. Each rotation event is logged.
[10:17] Mark: Any gotchas for SCIM when provisioning users with complex groups? We have nested groups.
[10:21] Ethan: SCIM handles groups but nested groups can get tricky; we'll test with your Okta config in pilot.
[10:28] Samir: For cost estimates, could you ballpark hosted vs dedicated for our expected 200 req/s baseline?
[10:34] Ethan: We'll provide a formal price sheet but ballpark: hosted is cheaper TCO initially but Dedicated gives predictable unit costs at scale and better p95 consistency. We'll send a comparative sheet.
[10:43] Mark: Perfect. Anything else on security?
[10:46] Lena: One last thing — if we choose Hosted with CMK, will Redwood have any admin ability over the key itself? We need zero ability for provider to decrypt without our explicit allow.
[10:56] Priya: If the CMK lives in your account, Redwood has no direct access. If it's hosted CMK, we maintain controls but can restrict access; we'll outline exact key policy examples.
[11:08] Ethan: Alright I'm going to recap next steps. We'll send SOC2/ISO links, security deck, sample audit logs, Dedicated pilot plan, and pricing.
[11:17] Mark: Thanks. Sounds good. We'll get Samir the traffic and prompts and Lena will surface retention policy.
[11:25] Tara: We'll review DPA and follow-up on contract language.
[11:29] Ethan: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with artifacts.
[11:33] Priya: Thanks all.
[11:36] [call ends]
